text:
If tonight's your last easy outdoor evening for a bit, get out and enjoy it. Skies are mostly cloudy but calm, still 84 as the sun goes down at 8:18, and it'll stay mild overnight with a low near 71 and just a light south breeze. The lake's sitting quiet too, waves 1 to 2 feet, water a warm 77, so a late paddle or dockside dinner is a fine call.

Sunday's the pivot. NWS has showers and storms holding off until afternoon with just a 30% chance, but the European model is much wetter, near certain on rain by Sunday, and I'd lean that way given how the forecasters' own reasoning has been trending wetter too. Plan an earlier lake outing if you've got one, winds will pick up to 15 knots with gusts near 30 by afternoon. The heaviest rain looks aimed at New York and Canada, so Burlington should see showers and a rumble of thunder rather than anything severe, but Sunday night into Monday keep the umbrella handy, better than half a chance of steady rain overnight.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST: BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - The first day of August will feature pleasant weather for today with morning sunshine followed by increasing high clouds. It will be warm and moderately humid with highs in the 80s. Sunday and Monday will feature active, wet weather, though it’s looking less impactful than originally forecast. Showers will move into New York Sunday morning, possibly spreading into western parts of Vermont. There is the chance for a thunderstorm, but severe weather isn’t expected. However, some heavy downpours are possible Sunday night, though the heaviest rain is now expected to remain to our northwest in Canada. Parts of New York may get up to an inch of rain with isolated flash flooding not out of the question in the St. Lawrence Valley. Smaller amounts are expected for Vermont and New Hampshire.
